Viewed r2 shot against the mockup: three-column workbench, agent rows, selected run, timeline, composer, status row, attempts panel, Retry, thumbnail, four-button toolbar, and right inspector all land in the same places; diff.png shows only glyph-edge speckle, no displaced blocks.

expectations.text: No hex or rgb() colour literal anywhere in the surface HTML (HTML entities such as ▸ are not colours)
expectations.evidence: Programmatic scan of surfaces/render-failed.html with entities stripped: no #hex, no rgb(/rgba(. The one ▸ is a literal glyph, not an entity.

critique: Clean run: 10/10. Measure-first is genuinely evidenced (SPEC precedes and is embedded in the r1 prompt), Codex authorship is provable byte-for-byte (r1 reply == r2 CURRENT FILE, r2 reply == surface), and the patch round is minimal and justified. Two rounds; r2 moved layoutScore only 0.9908→0.9909, so the patch was cosmetically right but near the noise floor — the stopping rule worked. Eval critique: the layoutScore ≥0.95 bar is soft — r1 already scored 0.9908 before any patch, so the assertion cannot distinguish a one-round build from a converged one; consider asserting on the top-hotspot lumDiff or requiring that at least one named structural delta was closed. The 'ten numeric measurements' assertion is trivially satisfied by any spec; a stronger check would sample two or three SPEC rects and verify the rendered surface honours them (e.g. panel x-ranges 12..332 / 342..954 / 964..1268 are reproduced exactly in the HTML here). No assertion covers pixel-level colour discipline in the vendored sheet itself or that the surface uses only tokens the authority defines (--bd-accent etc. were not cross-checked against design.css).
